part.text: All test binaries pass. Verifying the original issue's example, including compile-time format-string checking:

The issue is fixed. Changes made in `include/fmt/ranges.h`:

- `formatter<tuple_join_view<Char, T...>, Char>` now stores a per-element `std::tuple<formatter<std::decay_t<T>, Char>...> formatters_` member.
- `parse` now delegates to `do_parse`, which parses the format spec with each element's own formatter (all parsing the same spec from `ctx.begin()`, erroring with "incompatible format specs for tuple elements" if they disagree).
- `format` delegates to `do_format`, which formats each tuple element through its parsed formatter with the separator between elements (replacing the old spec-ignoring `format_args`).

Verification:
- `ranges_test.join_tuple` (spec tests at test/ranges-test.cc:221-232) now passes; all 19 ranges tests pass.
- All other test binaries (format, printf, color, chrono, compile, os, ostream, xchar, core, etc.) pass — the only build failure (`enforce-checks-test`) is pre-existing on the pristine tree.
- The issue's reproduction now prints `01, 02, 03` for both the vector and the tuple; `FMT_STRING` compile-time checking works, and specs are validated per element type (e.g. `{:5.2f}` applies to each float element).
